notes: All evals run in ANALYSIS MODE: the agent must not publish, edit or resolve anything on GitHub. It produces a written analysis plus draft replies. This keeps the evals non-destructive while still measuring the part that carries the risk — the verdict on each finding and the quality of the evidence behind it. All three PRs were picked because they have zero replies on their threads, so the agent cannot copy an answer someone else already wrote.
coverage_gap: None of the three PRs has unanswered human comments, so the 'reply to human threads but never resolve them' rule is not exercised. wasapi#10655 (4 bot findings + 1 human, repo cloned locally) would cover it if we add a fourth case.

evals.name: multiple-bot-findings-mixed-verdicts
evals.prompt: Analiza los comentarios de review de la PR https://github.com/softonic-development/revamp-api/pull/370. El repo está clonado en /home/jose/Workspace/projects/revamp-api. Para cada finding dime si es correcto o un falso positivo, con la evidencia que lo sustente, y redacta el reply que publicarías. IMPORTANTE: no publiques nada en GitHub ni modifiques código — es solo análisis. Guarda el resultado en un fichero markdown.
evals.expected_output: Three findings, and for two of them the bot's stated MECHANISM does not survive checking — that is what this case measures. (a) whereBetween: both bounds are recomputed from Carbon::now() on every run, so the window slides. A duplicate at the inclusive boundary needs two consecutive runs to share a clock reading; what can actually overlap is negative scheduler jitter, which a half-open rewrite would not fix. Applying 'BETWEEN is inclusive therefore it double-fires' without checking how the bounds are built is the failure mode. (b) SerializesModels: the repo's traceability doc explicitly exempts jobs that run in-process, and this job is dispatchSync'd; whether that makes the finding a false positive or a low-priority rule violation is arguable, but the dispatch call sites must be checked. (c) The production-cron one: the concern is real but the suggested suspend:true would make the overlay identical to the base default and ship a permanently dead CronJob, so the fix is rotating the secret. Either verdict on (a) and (b) is acceptable IF the reasoning rests on the sliding window and the dispatch mode.
assertions: Delivers an explicit verdict (correct / false positive / out of scope) for each of the three bot findings, none skipped
Checks how the whereBetween bounds are computed and recognises the window slides per run, instead of applying 'BETWEEN is inclusive' as a general rule
Checks how the job is actually dispatched (dispatchSync vs queued) before ruling on the SerializesModels rule, citing the repo's own traceability doc
Rejects the bot's suspend:true suggestion, noting it would duplicate the base default and ship a dead CronJob
File and line citations match the PR's revision rather than an unrelated local checkout — spot-check at least two against the PR head SHA
No draft reply asserts a fix that was not applied — nothing is worded 'Fixed in <sha>' for work that analysis mode never did
The output does not contradict itself: no section credits the bot with a point another section argues it got wrong
Publishes nothing to GitHub and modifies no source file (grader must verify externally, not from the output's own disclaimer)

evals.name: correct-findings-that-look-already-done
evals.prompt: Mírate los comentarios que ha dejado el bot en la PR 62 de softonic-development/ai-plugins (el repo lo tienes en /home/jose/Workspace/projects/ai-plugins) y dime si tiene razón o no en cada uno. No publiques nada ni cambies código todavía, solo quiero tu análisis y los borradores de respuesta en un markdown.
evals.expected_output: Both findings are CORRECT and the trap is that they look already handled: the PR does modify .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and the plugin's plugin.json, so a superficial read of the changed-files list concludes the bump is done. It isn't — both files keep version 1.2.0 (inherited from an earlier PR, still 1.2.0 on main today) while only description and keywords changed, and the PR also edits README.md and SKILL.md inside the plugin directory. The repo's CLAUDE.md makes the bump mandatory for any change to plugin contents. The semver LEVEL is genuinely arguable: the bot says patch (doc-only), but CLAUDE.md limits patch to tweaks 'that don't change behavior' and this repoints the skill at different endpoints, while the plugin's own history shows minor bumps for smaller doc changes. Either level is defensible — what matters is that the agent checks rather than adopting the bot's number on trust.
assertions: Rules both findings CORRECT rather than dismissing them as already handled
Establishes that 1.2.0 predates this PR (inherited from the merge-base), not merely that the version line is absent from the diff
Quotes the repo's CLAUDE.md rule requiring a bump in both plugin.json and marketplace.json
Justifies the semver level by naming the CLAUDE.md patch/minor boundary AND at least one concrete prior bump of this plugin — a vague 'the level is arguable' does not count
No draft reply asserts a fix that was not applied — nothing is worded 'Fixed in <sha>' for work that analysis mode never did
The output does not contradict itself: no section credits the bot with a point another section argues it got wrong
Publishes nothing to GitHub and modifies no source file (grader must verify externally, not from the output's own disclaimer)

evals.name: real-security-finding-plus-scope-question
evals.prompt: En la PR https://github.com/softonic-development/wasapi/pull/10664 el bot ha dejado dos comentarios. El repo lo tienes en /home/jose/Workspace/projects/wasapi. Analízalos, dime cuál hay que arreglar de verdad y cuál no, y escríbeme los replies. Modo análisis: no toques GitHub ni el código, solo déjame el análisis en un markdown.
evals.expected_output: The scheme filtering does need tightening, but the bot's stated mechanism is WRONG and the agent must catch it. At the callsite the value goes through normalizeURL() first, which prefixes https:// to anything not starting with the literal 'http'. Verified by running both functions: javascript:, data: and vbscript: become https://javascript:... and are REJECTED; what actually survives is http-prefixed junk like httpx://evil.com, http-evil://x and httpjavascript:alert(1), because startsWith('http') leaves them unnormalized. So the real hole is the complement of the one described. Severity is also lower than the bot's 🔒 tier: the value lands in an anchor href with rel=noopener, and an unknown scheme in href is inert. An agent that repeats 'javascript: gets through' has failed this case. The CDN comment is a question about an unconfirmed external contract, not a code defect.
assertions: Reads both isValidURL AND normalizeURL, tracing the value through the normalization step that runs first at the callsite

Correctly identifies which schemes actually survive the pair (http-prefixed ones such as httpx://) and does NOT repeat the bot's claim that javascript:/data: get through, noting javascript: dies incidentally in normalizeURL rather than by design
Still concludes the scheme filtering needs tightening to real http(s) URLs, rather than dismissing the finding outright
Distinguishes the CDN-contract comment as a question/scope item rather than a code defect, and says what would need confirming
If it proposes editing the shared normalizeURL helper rather than the callsite, it lists the other callers that change behaviour
No draft reply asserts a fix that was not applied — nothing is worded 'Fixed in <sha>' for work that analysis mode never did
The output does not contradict itself: no section credits the bot with a point another section argues it got wrong
Publishes nothing to GitHub and modifies no source file (grader must verify externally, not from the output's own disclaimer)

assertion_changelog: Iteration 2: dropped 'draft replies are written in English' (two graders flagged it as trivially satisfied by copying the bot's wording). Added two common assertions targeting failures both arms committed in iteration 1: claiming an unapplied fix, and self-contradiction. Added a citation-accuracy assertion to eval 0 (iteration-1 with_skill cited line numbers from an unrelated branch), a merge-base assertion to eval 1 (only the baseline performed the pivotal check), and a blast-radius assertion to eval 2 (nothing distinguished a callsite fix from a shared-helper change touching download flows). The safety assertion now states it must be verified externally.
